questions.stem: Where and when does The Namesake begin?
options: In New York in 1994, as Gogol starts work at an architecture firm
In Ohio in 1999, as Ashoke begins a year of teaching at a university
In Cambridge, Massachusetts, in 1968, as Ashima waits to give birth
In Calcutta in 1960, as Ashoke and Ashima first meet before marrying
questions.explanation: The novel opens in 1968 in Cambridge, where Ashoke is studying at MIT and Ashima is about to give birth far from her family in Calcutta.

questions.stem: Why do Ashoke and Ashima first name their son Gogol?
options: Ashoke hopes that his son will grow up to become a famous writer like the Russian author himself
It was the name of Ashoke's own father, who had died shortly before the boy was born
The hospital needs a name, and the letter with his great-grandmother's choice never arrives
Ashima's mother chose the name over the telephone from Calcutta on the day he was born
questions.explanation: By Bengali custom an elder chooses the name, but Ashima's grandmother's letter is lost. The hospital will not release the baby without a name, so Ashoke offers Gogol as a pet name.

questions.stem: What happened to Ashoke as a young man in India?
options: He survived a train crash, found because rescuers heard him calling for help
He lost his job, and a professor helped him to find a new post in America
He survived a train crash, found because he was holding a page of a Gogol story
He was hurt in a riot, and a stranger carried him to safety through the streets of Calcutta
questions.explanation: Ashoke was reading Nikolai Gogol's stories when his train was wrecked. Rescuers found him because of the page of 'The Overcoat' in his hand, which is why the name means so much to him.

questions.stem: When Gogol starts kindergarten, what happens with the name Nikhil?
options: The school will not accept Nikhil because it is not on his birth certificate
His teacher shortens Nikhil to Nick, and the nickname stays with him for years
His parents want the school to use Nikhil, but he answers only to Gogol
He insists on being called Nikhil, but his parents make the school use Gogol
questions.explanation: Ashoke and Ashima choose Nikhil as his 'good name' for school, but the little boy refuses it. The school lets him stay Gogol, a choice he later resents.

questions.stem: What does Ashoke give Gogol for his fourteenth birthday?
options: A book of Nikolai Gogol's short stories
A camera for photographing buildings
A train ticket to visit his grandparents
An old overcoat that belonged to Ashoke
questions.explanation: Ashoke gives him the stories of the writer he was named after. Gogol, uninterested, puts the book away, and Ashoke holds back from telling him about the crash.

questions.stem: What does Gogol do just before he starts at Yale?
options: He travels alone to Calcutta to meet relatives
He moves into Maxine's family home in New York
He travels to Russia to learn about the writer he is named after
He legally changes his first name to Nikhil
questions.explanation: Gogol goes to court to become Nikhil, hoping a new name will make him a new person. At university almost no one knows him as Gogol.

questions.stem: What finally prompts Ashoke to tell Gogol the story behind his name?
options: Gogol's train home from university is delayed, and Ashoke grows worried
Gogol finds a newspaper report of the crash among his father's papers
Gogol asks why his father chose to study engineering at MIT in America
Gogol tells his father that he plans to marry Maxine and leave Boston
questions.explanation: When Gogol's train is held up because a man has jumped in front of it, Ashoke waits anxiously. Afterwards he finally tells his son about the crash, and Gogol is shaken.

questions.stem: Gogol's attraction to Maxine is bound up with:
options: her wealthy family's relaxed, confident American way of life
his parents' strong wish that he marry a Bengali woman like her
her wish to learn Bengali and move with him to Calcutta
their work together as architects at the same New York firm
questions.explanation: Gogol moves into Maxine's parents' house and enjoys their ease and openness. Being with them is also a way of escaping his own family.

questions.stem: How does Ashoke die?
options: Suddenly, of a heart attack, while working away from home in Ohio
After a long illness, at the family home on Pemberton Road near Boston
In a car accident while driving to visit Gogol in New York
During a family trip to Calcutta, after catching a fever
questions.explanation: Ashoke dies of a heart attack while on a temporary university posting in Ohio. Gogol travels there to identify him and clear his apartment.

questions.stem: What effect does Ashoke's death have on Gogol?
options: He resents his mother for observing the Bengali mourning rituals
He draws closer to his mother and sister and drifts away from Maxine
He moves to Calcutta to live with his father's brothers and sisters
He grows closer to Maxine, who helps him through the months of his grief
questions.explanation: Grief pulls Gogol back toward his family and their rituals of mourning. Maxine cannot share that part of his life, and the relationship ends.

questions.stem: How does Gogol come to date Moushumi?
options: Maxine introduces them at a party at her parents' house
They work together on a building design in New York
His mother urges him to contact her, the daughter of family friends
They meet by chance on a train between New Haven and Boston one weekend
questions.explanation: Ashima suggests he call Moushumi, whom he knew as a child at Bengali gatherings. He agrees partly to please his mother, and they fall for each other.

questions.stem: Why does Gogol and Moushumi's marriage end?
options: Gogol meets Maxine again by chance and returns to her in New York
Moushumi's parents insist that she leave Gogol and move to Paris
Gogol decides to move to Calcutta, and Moushumi refuses to go
Moushumi feels trapped in the marriage and has an affair with Dimitri
questions.explanation: Moushumi, who has also tried to escape her Bengali upbringing, comes to feel the marriage is a retreat into it. Her affair with Dimitri ends the marriage.

questions.stem: What does Ashima decide to do after Ashoke's death?
options: Remarry and settle permanently in Massachusetts
Move in with Sonia and Ben and stay in America permanently
Divide her time between India and the United States
Sell the house and move into Gogol's flat in New York
questions.explanation: Ashima sells the house on Pemberton Road and plans to spend part of each year in each country. She has become someone at home in both places.

questions.stem: How does the novel end?
options: In Ohio, Gogol scatters his father's ashes and changes his name back to Gogol
In New York, Gogol and Moushumi agree to try again in a new apartment together
At the last Christmas Eve party at Pemberton Road, Gogol begins to read his father's gift
At Sonia's wedding in Calcutta, Gogol gives a long speech about his father's life and death
questions.explanation: At the family's final party in the house, Gogol finds the book of stories and starts to read. The ending suggests he is ready, at last, to accept his name and his father's story.

questions.stem: Who is Ashima?
options: Gogol's great-grandmother, who chose his good name
Gogol's mother, a Bengali migrant homesick in America
Gogol's sister, a paralegal who becomes engaged to Ben
Gogol's wife, who studies French literature in New York
questions.explanation: Ashima arrives in Cambridge after an arranged marriage and misses Calcutta deeply. Sonia is Gogol's sister and Moushumi his wife.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes Ashoke?
options: Strict and harsh, he refuses to let Gogol change his name
Restless and unhappy, he longs to leave his family for India
Quiet, bookish and devoted, he rarely shows his deepest feelings
Loud and sociable, he loves telling everyone his life story
questions.explanation: Ashoke keeps the story of the crash to himself for years. He even lets Gogol change his name, though the name means more to him than his son knows.

questions.stem: How does Ashima change over the course of the novel?
options: From a devout follower of tradition to someone who rejects Bengali customs
From a homesick newcomer to a woman who chooses to stay in Massachusetts permanently
From a lonely, dependent newcomer to an independent woman at home in two countries
From an independent woman to one who depends on her children after Ashoke dies
questions.explanation: At first Ashima is isolated and afraid. By the end she has built a community, coped with Ashoke's death and chosen a life divided between Calcutta and America.

questions.stem: How does Sonia differ from Gogol?
options: She seems more at ease moving between American and Bengali life
She feels more pressure than Gogol to marry a Bengali man
She resents her name and changes it before going to college
She studies architecture and joins Gogol's firm in New York
questions.explanation: Sonia is comfortable with her American identity and stays close to the family, especially after Ashoke dies. Gogol's struggle with his name has no real parallel in her.

questions.stem: In what way is Moushumi a mirror of Gogol?
options: She too lost a parent suddenly while she was at university
She too changed her name in court before going to college
She too has spent years trying to escape her Bengali upbringing
She too was named after a Russian writer by her own father
questions.explanation: Moushumi has built a life around French literature, Paris and New York, away from her parents' world. Marrying Gogol feels to her like going back, which is part of why it fails.

questions.stem: At a dinner party, Moushumi tells her friends that Gogol was once called Gogol. Why does this hurt him?
options: It reveals that she has told her parents about their marriage problems
It shows that she has secretly been in touch with Maxine
It surprises him, because he thought he had kept the name a secret from her
It exposes a private part of his past that he has tried to leave behind
questions.explanation: Moushumi knew him as a child, so she knows the name. Telling it to strangers for amusement shows how little she shares his feelings about it.

questions.stem: Where do Ashoke and Ashima come from?
options: Bombay, on the west coast
Delhi, the national capital
Madras, in the far south
Calcutta, in West Bengal
questions.explanation: The Gangulis are Bengalis from Calcutta (now Kolkata). Bengali language, food and customs shape the family's life in America.

questions.stem: In Bengali tradition, what is the difference between a pet name and a good name?
options: A pet name is given by a priest; a good name by the parents
A pet name is used at home; a good name is for the outside world
A pet name is chosen by the child; a good name by the teacher
A pet name is used in public; a good name is kept secret
questions.explanation: The pet name (daknam) is for family and friends; the good name (bhalonam) goes on documents and at school. Gogol's trouble begins because his pet name becomes his official name.

questions.stem: Why do the Gangulis spend so much time with other Bengali families in America?
options: They are required to meet as members of the same university department
They have agreed to return to India together once their children grow up
They run a small business together in the town outside Boston
They build a community that keeps their language, food and customs alive
questions.explanation: The Bengali gatherings replace the extended family the parents left behind. For Gogol and Sonia, though, they can feel like an obligation.

questions.stem: The novel covers about thirty years, from 1968 to 2000. Why does this matter?
options: It follows a migrant family from arrival to the children's adulthood
It shows how India changed from British rule to independence and after
It records the whole history of Bengali migration since 1900
It traces Gogol's career from student to retired architect
questions.explanation: The long time span lets Lahiri show both generations: the parents adapting to a new country and the children growing up between two cultures.

questions.stem: Which theme is most central to The Namesake?
options: How a father's ambitions decide the course of his son's career
How names shape, and fail to capture, a person's identity
How migrants must give up their own culture to succeed in America
How arranged marriages bring stability to migrant families
questions.explanation: Gogol's name ties him to a Russian writer, a Bengali custom and his father's secret. His struggle with it is a struggle over who he is.

questions.stem: Gogol hopes becoming Nikhil will make him a new person. What does the novel suggest?
options: A new name changes little, since most people he meets still call him Gogol
A new name brings him closer to his father, who chose it for him
A new name changes how others see him but cannot erase his past or family
A new name frees him from his past once he moves away from home
questions.explanation: As Nikhil he feels freer, but his family still call him Gogol and he never fully feels like Nikhil. Only after his father's death does he begin to understand what Gogol means.

questions.stem: How does the novel present the relationship between migrant parents and their children?
options: With ease, as the children slip happily between their two cultures
With distance, as the parents leave their children's upbringing to schools
With love and misunderstanding, as each generation wants a different life
With resentment, as the parents blame their children for losing Bengali ways
questions.explanation: Ashoke and Ashima want their children to keep Bengali ways; Gogol wants to be American. The gap is painful but never loveless, and it narrows by the end.

questions.stem: What does the novel suggest about home and belonging?
options: Home is the place where a person was born, whatever happens later
Home matters little to migrants, who quickly forget where they came from
Home is found through marriage to someone from the same culture
Home can be divided between places, as Ashima's is between two countries
questions.explanation: Ashima ends the novel at home in both Calcutta and America. Gogol's failed marriage to Moushumi shows that a shared background alone does not make a home.

questions.stem: In which tense and person is The Namesake mostly written?
options: The present tense, in the first person
The past tense, in the third person
The present tense, in the third person
The past tense, in the first person
questions.explanation: Lahiri narrates in the third person and the present tense. The present tense gives even events decades apart a sense of immediacy.

questions.stem: How does the narrative point of view move through the novel?
options: It is told by Sonia, who describes her brother's life from a distance
It begins with Moushumi, then moves to Gogol after their wedding
It begins with Ashima and Ashoke, then follows Gogol for most of the book
It is told by Gogol throughout, looking back from old age on his life
questions.explanation: The opening chapters show the parents' experience of migration. The focus then shifts to Gogol, though Lahiri returns to Ashima near the end.

questions.stem: In what way is the novel's structure circular?
options: It opens with Ashima in her kitchen and closes with her last party in the family home
It opens and closes with Gogol on a train between New Haven and his parents' home
It opens and closes with Ashoke reading Nikolai Gogol's stories
It opens with Ashoke's death and then moves back to tell the story of his life
questions.explanation: The novel begins with Ashima preparing food in Cambridge and ends at a family party before she leaves the house. Gogol finally opening his father's gift completes the circle.

questions.stem: What does the book of Gogol stories come to symbolise?
options: Gogol's secret ambition to become a writer instead of working as an architect
Ashima's homesickness for the books she left behind in Calcutta
Ashima's loneliness in the years after her husband's death
The bond between father and son, and the history Gogol had refused to know
questions.explanation: The book is Ashoke's gift and connects to the night that saved his life. When Gogol finally reads it, he is reaching back to his father.

questions.stem: Trains recur through the novel. What do they often mark?
options: Gogol's love of travel, which shapes his work as an architect
Ashima's freedom, as she travels alone across America by train
Turning points, from Ashoke's crash to the night Gogol learns his name's story
Moments of escape, as characters flee their families in search of new lives abroad
questions.explanation: A train crash changes Ashoke's life, and a delayed train leads him to tell Gogol the truth. Journeys in the novel are bound up with change.

questions.stem: Who says, 'You remind me of everything that followed.'?
options: Moushumi, when Gogol asks about her years living in Paris
Maxine, when Gogol asks whether she still thinks of him
Ashoke, when Gogol asks if he reminds him of the crash
Ashima, when Gogol asks about her first years in America
questions.explanation: Gogol asks whether he reminds his father of that terrible night. Ashoke's answer shows that he sees his son as part of the life he was given after surviving.

questions.stem: Being a foreigner, for Ashima, is described as 'a sort of lifelong pregnancy'. What idea does this express?
options: Ashima's pride in raising children who feel fully American
Migrant life as a constant wait and burden that never comes to an end
Ashima's joy at being pregnant with her first child in a new country
Ashima's belief that she will soon return home to Calcutta for good
questions.explanation: Like pregnancy, being foreign draws curiosity and feels like a perpetual waiting. Unlike pregnancy, it never ends, which captures Ashima's lasting sense of displacement.

questions.stem: Ashoke tells Gogol, 'We all came out of Gogol's overcoat.' When does he say it?
options: In hospital in Ohio, shortly before he dies of a heart attack
On Gogol's fourteenth birthday, when giving him the book of stories
On the night of the train crash, to a stranger in his compartment
At Gogol's graduation, when the family celebrate his new degree
questions.explanation: Ashoke repeats a saying attributed to Dostoyevsky about Gogol's influence. For Gogol it means little yet; for Ashoke it hides a far more personal meaning.

questions.stem: For the question 'How does The Namesake explore the ways names shape identity?', which is the strongest topic sentence?
options: The Namesake is a novel by Jhumpa Lahiri that was published in 2003 and made into a film
Lahiri shows that Gogol's name carries a family history he must accept before he can know himself
In The Namesake, Gogol Ganguli is born in Cambridge, Massachusetts, to Bengali parents in 1968
This essay will discuss how names are shown in the novel The Namesake by Jhumpa Lahiri
questions.explanation: A strong topic sentence answers the question and names what the paragraph will prove. The others retell, announce or state facts without making an argument.

questions.stem: A student writes: 'Gogol changes his name to Nikhil before he goes to Yale.' How could this be turned into analysis?
options: Add the name of the court, the judge, and the exact date on which the change took place
Quote the judge's question about why he wants to change his name
Describe the train journey he takes to New Haven at the start of term
Explain how the change shows his wish to escape his family, and why it cannot work
questions.explanation: Analysis explains what an event suggests. Linking the name change to Gogol's divided identity, and to his later return to the name, connects it to the novel's ideas.
